chunks: They did not precede Him in speech, and they act on His command.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that angels do not precede Allah in speech?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the absolute subordination of the angels to Allah's will, distinguishing them from humans who possess free will. It highlights their role as obedient servants who do not precede Him in speech or action, serving as a model of perfect submission. This concept is often linked to the broader theme of divine authority and the hierarchy of creation.
